sentences.text: Ilokelesia was a medium-sized theropod dinosaur known for distinctive features in its quadrate and postorbital skull bones. Its vertebrae also show unique traits, such as reduced processes on the neck bones and a lack of pleurocoels on the back vertebrae.
The species name aguadagrandensis refers to the specific locality Aguada Grande where the fossil was found.
A 2016 analysis estimated Ilokelesia to be 5.3 meters long.

Fossils of Ilokelesia were found in the Early Cretaceous Huincul Formation in Neuquén Province, Argentina. The animal is known only from very fragmentary skull, axial, and appendicular skeleton elements discovered in 1991.
The only known specimen was described by Rodolfo Coria and Leonardo Salgado in late 1998. These fossils were discovered ten meters away from the holotype of Huinculsaurus.
Ilokelesia is classified in the family Abelisauridae.
A subsequent analysis placed Ilokelesia within Abelisauridae as a brachyrostran carnotaurine.
Ilokelesia lived in South America during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 98 to 90 million years ago.
The fossil record for Ilokelesia spans from 110.1 to 106.3 million years ago during the Albian stage.
